title: Extreme-point question for the feedback vertex set LP
statement_utf8: Does every basic feasible solution to the LP formulation for Feedback Vertex Set suggested by Chudak, Goemans, Hochbaum, and Williamson [10] have a variable with value at least $1/2$ (for non-trivial instances)?

title: Spohn’s central-limit conjecture for the fixed-coupling Fröhlich polaron
statement_utf8: For every fixed coupling $\alpha>0$, as $T\to\infty$, the diffusively rescaled Brownian path under the Polaron measure should become asymptotically Gaussian with mean zero and variance $\sigma^2(\alpha)>0$.

technical_disposition: Requires a uniform-in-time probabilistic limit and positive diffusion constant. Small-path computations would not settle this; no bounded full-scope mechanism.

title: Existence of a bilinear form for the \(E_{11}\) tensor-hierarchy representation
statement_utf8: Does the representation carried by the infinite collection of field strengths \(F^I\), as defined through the tensor-hierarchy superalgebra \(T(\mathfrak e_{11})\), admit a \(K(E_{11})\)-invariant symmetric bilinear form \(\eta_{IJ}\)?

statement_utf8: Conjecture: The field-strength representation carrying the components \(F^I\) admits a \(K(E_{11})\)-invariant symmetric bilinear form \(\eta_{IJ}\), as required in the first-order equation \(\eta_{IJ}F^J=\Omega_{IJ}F^J\).

title: Endoscopic transfer of Arthur’s stable distributions via normalized vanishing cycles
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be $\mathrm{GL}_n$, $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$, or $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and let $\psi$ be a local Arthur parameter with corresponding Langlands parameter $\phi_\psi$. For every semisimple $s\in Z_{\widehat G}(\psi)$, the endoscopic transfer of Arthur’s stable distributions is calculated by normalized vanishing cycles:
\[
\eta_{\psi,s}=\eta^{\mathrm{NEvs}}_{\phi_\psi,s}.
\]
classification_reason: Local field and NEvs normalization are not defined.
quantifiers: All listed classical groups, local Arthur parameters and semisimple centralizer elements.
technical_disposition: Equality of stable distributions needs the full endoscopic normalization bridge. A test parameter would be only a helper; no short all-parameter mechanism.

title: Volume maximization for convolution bodies
statement_utf8: Is there a value of $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that $|C_\delta K|_n\le |C_\delta B_K|_n$ for every symmetric convex body $K$? Here $C_\delta K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_K(x)\ge\delta|K|_n\}$, $g_K(x)=|K\cap(K+x)|_n$, and $B_K$ is the Euclidean ball having the same volume as $K$.
classification_reason: The dimension quantifier and whether delta may depend on dimension are not explicit.
quantifiers: Exist delta in (0,1), then for every centrally symmetric convex K the convolution-body volume is bounded by that for the equal-volume ball.
technical_disposition: Comparing cubes and balls for one delta cannot refute existence of some delta. No uniform-in-delta obstruction identified.

title: Measure comparison for dilations with an intersection-body density
statement_utf8:
Let \bc be a log-concave measure on \c3n such that its density is given by $d\bc(x)=e^{-\(\x\_M)}\,dx$, where $M$ is an intersection body. Consider convex symmetric bodies $K,L\subset \c3n$ satisfying
$$\bc(tK\cap \u0006\^\)\le \bc(tL\cap \u0006\^\)\qquad\text{for all }\u0006\\in S^{n-1}\text{ and all }t>0.$$
Does it follow that $\bc(K)\le \bc(L)$?
classification_reason: Ambient space, density exponent and hyperplane notation are corrupted.
quantifiers: Intended all positive dilations and all hyperplane directions, followed by total-measure comparison.
technical_disposition: Do not silently reconstruct the corrupted measure problem as a standard Busemann-Petty statement. No valid literal computation or replacement.

title: Affine quermassintegral inequality over real, complex, and quaternionic spaces
statement_utf8:
For every convex body $K\subseteq \mathbb{F}^n$ with non-empty interior, where $\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H}\}$, $p=\dim_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{F}\in\{1,2,4\}$, and $m\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, 
$$|K|^{-m}\ge \frac{(\kappa_{mp})^n}{(\kappa_{np})^m}\int_{\operatorname{Gr}_m(n,\mathbb{F})}|P_EK|^{-n}\,dE,$$
with equality if and only if $K$ is a real, complex, or quaternionic ellipsoid.
classification_reason: Standard volumes, projections, Grassmannian probability measure and unit-ball constants give a closed mathematical inequality.
quantifiers: All real/complex/quaternionic convex bodies with interior and every 1<=m<n; includes equality characterization.
technical_disposition: Ball substitution gives equality, but does not address the universal bound. The quaternionic and equality clauses prevent reducing this to one real parameter case; no full route.

title: Bevan's Conjecture 1 on scaling limits of pattern-avoiding permutations
statement_utf8: **Conjecture 1 (Bevan, Dijon 2023).** If every pattern in $B$ ends in $1$, then the scaling limit of $\\operatorname{Av}(B)$ is the increasing permuton.
classification_reason: Nonempty basis and existence of arbitrarily large avoiders are not stipulated.
quantifiers: For every eligible basis B ending in 1, the uniform random avoider has increasing permuton limit.
technical_disposition: Primary passage gives inversion-density expectation tending to zero as a sufficient route. Empty basis or a length-one forbidden pattern is only a wording objection, not eligible credit. No expectation bound obtained.

title: Rationality converse for subclasses of the separable permutations
statement_utf8: If a subclass of the separable permutations contains all of $\operatorname{Av}(231)$ or one of its symmetries, must it have a nonrational generating function?
classification_reason: Standard permutation-class containment and ordinary counting generating functions fix the predicate.
quantifiers: Every subclass of separables containing Av(231) or a symmetry has nonrational generating function.
technical_disposition: Primary Question 4 matches. Catalan containment provides a coefficient lower bound, which does not imply nonrationality of a larger class. Strong rationality theorem is a different implication, no subsumption bridge claimed.

title: Structure of subclasses of the separable permutations
statement_utf8: Let $C$ be a subclass of the separable permutations. Then either $C$ is sum or skew closed (or a finite union of such classes), or $C \subseteq X[U]$, where $X=\operatorname{Av}(2413,3142,2143,3412)$ and $U$ is a proper subclass of $C$. Here, $X[U]$ denotes the permutation class obtained by replacing points of permutations in $X$ by sequences order-isomorphic to elements of $U$.
classification_reason: Both the containing class and inflation operation are specified with standard sum/skew closure.
quantifiers: Every separable subclass has one of the stated closure alternatives or admits a proper subclass U with C contained in X[U].
technical_disposition: A finite basis sample cannot witness failure of every possible proper U; needs structural decomposition across the entire class. No short route.

title: Inversion monotonicity conjecture for \[4mAv(1324)\[0m
statement_utf8: For the permutation class \(\operatorname{Av}(1324)\), if \(k\) is fixed, then the number of permutations with exactly \(k\) inversions grows monotonically with the size of the permutation.
classification_reason: Classical pattern avoidance, inversion number and weak monotonic growth have standard meanings.
quantifiers: For every fixed k and every n, a(n+1,k)>=a(n,k) in Av(1324).
technical_disposition: Appending a maximum preserves inversion count but can complete a 132 pattern to 1324. Thus the obvious injection fails; no replacement injection established.

title: Bevan’s permuton-limit conjecture for layered avoidance classes
statement_utf8: For every non-empty permutation $\alpha$, the permuton limit of $\operatorname{Av}(\alpha \mathbin{\ominus} 1)$ is the diagonal permuton.
classification_reason: Skew sum, avoidance and diagonal permuton have standard definitions.
quantifiers: For every nonempty permutation alpha, the uniform Av(alpha skew-sum 1) has diagonal limit.
technical_disposition: One-pattern subfamily of the limit-shape issue; monotone alpha cases do not imply all alpha. No inversion-density control for arbitrary alpha.

title: Non-\D-finiteness of the generating function for \coperatorname{Av}(4123,4231,4312)
statement_utf8: Let $A(0,t)$ be the generating function for the permutation class $\operatorname{Av}(4123,4231,4312)$. Is $A(0,t)$ non-$D$-finite?

quantifiers: Non-D-finiteness of the full Av(4123,4231,4312) series.

title: Combinatorial interpretation of analytically extended k-arrangement moments
statement_utf8:
Extend the definition of $A(n,k)$ by
\[
A(n,k)=\int_{k-1}^{\infty} x^n e^{-x+(k-1)}\,dx
\]
to $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $k\in\mathbb{R}$. Does $A(n,k)$ have a combinatorial interpretation when $k$ is an arbitrary negative integer?
classification_reason: Combinatorial interpretation does not specify unsigned sets versus signed or weighted objects.
quantifiers: Every n and every negative integer k admit the requested interpretation of the integral.
technical_disposition: Primary passage already separates the even nonnegative case. Exact calculation A(1,-1)=-1 rules out unsigned counts only; signed fixed-point polynomial interpretations are routine and supply no eligible result.

title: Bouvel’s k-shuffle conjecture
statement_utf8: **Conjecture 1.** For a fixed $k\in\mathbb{N}$, any sufficiently long permutation contains a factor which is a $k$-shuffle of $12$ or $21$. Here, a $k$-shuffle of a permutation $\tau$ is a permutation of length $k|\tau|$ whose elements can be partitioned into $k$ sub-permutations, each with shape $\tau$.
classification_reason: The shuffle operation is explicitly defined and factor means a contiguous block.
quantifiers: For each k there exists N(k) such that every permutation of length >=N(k) contains the specified 2k-factor.
technical_disposition: Primary body reduces this to acyclicity of a (2k-1)!-vertex factor graph and reports verification through k=5. Rechecking those cases earns no credit; no symbolic all-k acyclicity argument.

title: Generalizing Llarull stability to Goette–Semmelmann results

statement_utf8: There exist functions $f(k)=O(k\log k)$ and $g(d)=O(d)$ such that, for all positive integers $k$ and $d$, every graph $G$ contains either a family of $k$ cycles whose pairwise distance is more than $d$, or a set $X$ of at most $f(k)$ vertices such that $G-B_G(X,g(d))$ is a forest.
classification_reason: Distance, graph balls, cycles and forests are standard and all required asymptotic dependences are specified.

statement_utf8: For every prime power $q$, all $k,s\in\mathbb{N}$, and every $s$-colouring $c_0$ of $\operatorname{PG}(k-1,q)$, there exist $\delta,C>0$ such that, for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $c_0$-free colouring $c$ of $G\cong\operatorname{PG}(n-1,q)$, there is a subspace of $G$ with dimension at least $Cn^\delta$ that uses at most $s-1$ colours.

title: Alternating-group case of Kourovka Notebook Problem 19.12

title: Maglione’s conjecture on isomorphism classes of unipotent groups from elliptic curves
statement_utf8: Let $G_q$ be the collection of groups $G_{E,P}(\fF_q)$ arising from elliptic curves $E:y^2=x^3+ax+b$ with $a,b\in\u000cF_q$ and points $P\in E(\u000cF_q)$, where $G_{E,P}$ is the unipotent group scheme associated with $(E,P)$. Let $N_q=|G_q/\cong|$, the number of isomorphism classes of these groups. Conjecture: for every prime $p\ge 5$, $N_p=p^2+p-\gcd(p-2,3)+\gcd(p-1,4)$.

\]
where $G$ has nilpotency class $3$ and cardinality $p^{10}$? Here $E$ and $P$ range over the elliptic-curve/point data used to define $G_{E,P}(\mathbb F_p)$ in the report.

$$

title: An $L^p\to L^q$ fractal local smoothing conjecture
statement_utf8:
For every $1<p\le q<\infty$ with $q>p'$, the conjecture is that

\]
holds for all $j\ge 1$ whenever
\[
s>\frac{d+1}{2}\left(\frac1p-\frac1q\right)+\frac1q\,\nu_E^\sharp\!\left(\frac{q(d-1)}{2}\left(1-\frac1p-\frac1q\right)\right).
\]

title: Finite-direction characterization of GBD
statement_utf8:
Let $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be measurable. Assume that, for every $\xi\in W:=\{e_i:i=1,\ldots,d\}\cup\{e_i+e_j:1\le i<j\le d\}$, 
\[
\int_{\xi^\perp}\left(|D u_z^\xi|(\Omega_z^\xi\setminus J u_z^\xi)+\sum_{s\in J u_z^\xi}|u_z^\xi(s+0)-u_z^\xi(s-0)|\wedge 1\right)\,d\mathcal{H}^{d-1}(z)<+\infty.
\]
Then $u\in\mathrm{GBD}(\Omega)$.
classification_reason: Slice notation, domain assumptions and GBD conventions are not supplied.
quantifiers: Every measurable u satisfying all finitely many directional slice bounds lies in GBD.
technical_disposition: Need to reconstruct control in arbitrary directions from the specified finite set; scalar BV analogies do not establish the vector-valued slicing criterion.

title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture over \(\mathbb F_p\)
statement_utf8:

technical_disposition: The n=1 modulus-zero issue is a domain correction only. A handful of labelled trees would be parameter instances, not an all-tree construction.

title: Quasipolynomial bounds for the corners theorem
statement_utf8: Let $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and $A\subseteq [N]\times[N]$. Suppose that $A$ does not contain $(x,y)$, $(x+d,y)$, $(x,y+d)$ with $d\ne 0$. Then $|A|\ll N^2\exp\left(- (\log N)^{1/600}\right)$.
classification_reason: Grid, forbidden corners and uniform asymptotic bound are explicit.
quantifiers: All N and all corner-free A satisfy the displayed absolute-constant bound.
technical_disposition: The exact bound appears as Theorem 1 in the cited primary report, attributed to joint work with Jaber, Liu, Lovett and Ostuni. It is not eligible as a new conjecture resolution. Proof body beyond the report excerpt is unread.

title: Diameter of a directed Cayley graph of the symmetric group
statement_utf8:
The report conjectures that the diameter of the directed Cayley graph of $S_n$ generated by the left cyclic shift and the transposition of the first two elements is
\[
\frac{3n^2-8n+9}{4}\quad\text{for odd }n,
\qquad
\frac{3n^2-8n+12}{4}\quad\text{for even }n.
\]
classification_reason: Lower range of n is omitted.
quantifiers: Claimed odd/even diameter formula for the entire directed symmetric-group family.
technical_disposition: Exact BFS fails at n=2,3,4 and matches n=5..8. These are small-range objections only, not a substantive discovery. Primary formula found one PDF page earlier than the record locator; no all-n route or successor-body clearance.

title: Polishchuk–Van den Bergh semiorthogonal decomposition conjecture
statement_utf8: Suppose that $G$ is a finite group acting effectively on a smooth variety $X$ and that, for all $g\in G$, the geometric quotient $\bar X_g=X^g/C(g)$ is smooth. Then there is a semiorthogonal decomposition of $D_G(X)$ whose components $\mathcal C_{[g]}$ are in bijection with conjugacy classes and satisfy $\mathcal C_{[g]}\simeq D(\bar X_g)$.
classification_reason: Base field/characteristic and derived-category conventions are omitted.
quantifiers: Every effective finite group action with all smooth fixed-locus centralizer quotients admits the specified semiorthogonal decomposition.
technical_disposition: Positive-characteristic nonsemisimplicity may change the intended theorem. A characteristic-boundary correction receives no credit; no full derived-equivalence construction.

title: Sharpness of the realization-cardinality lower bound for monomial ideals
statement_utf8: The report conjectures that, for every realizable monomial ideal $I$ of $k[x_1,x_2]$, the lower bound $|D|\geq \max\{q:\operatorname{SH}^{q-1}(I\subset O)\neq 0\}$ for the cardinality of a realization $D$ is sharp; equivalently, some realization attains equality.
classification_reason: Realization D, ambient O and SH are undefined.
quantifiers: For every realizable monomial ideal in two variables, some realization attains the specified homological lower bound.
technical_disposition: A staircase diagram alone does not define the realization problem or its homology invariant. No bounded minimal realization certificate possible from this literal.

title: The Huang–Yang low-density expansion for the balanced spin-\[?]1/2 Fermi gas
statement_utf8:
For a spin-\[?]1/2 fermionic system in the thermodynamic, low-density regime with equal spin densities \(\rho_\uparrow=\rho_\downarrow=\rho/2\), the ground-state energy density is claimed to satisfy
\[
e(\rho/2,\rho/2)=\frac35(3\pi^2)^{2/3}\rho^{5/3}+2\pi a\rho^2+\frac{4(9\pi)^{2/3}}{35}(11-2\log 2)a^2\rho^{7/3}+o(\rho^{7/3}),\qquad \rho\to0.
\]
classification_reason: Hamiltonian, interaction-potential hypotheses, scattering length and limiting order are missing.
quantifiers: Balanced spin-half gas energy has the stated expansion through rho^(7/3) as density tends to zero.
technical_disposition: Coefficient matching cannot prove the uniform many-body error estimate. Need exact potential class and full thermodynamic limit; no finite-particle substitute.

title: Decategorified conjecture for unitary Yang–Baxter operators
statement_utf8: Let $(R,V)$ be a unitary solution to the Yang–Baxter equation. Then, for all $n$, the image $\rho_R(B_n)$ is a virtually abelian group; equivalently, $\rho_R(B_n)$ has a normal abelian subgroup of finite index.
classification_reason: Finite dimensionality, Hilbert setting and precise braid representation conventions are not explicit.
quantifiers: Every unitary Yang-Baxter pair and every n have virtually abelian braid image.
technical_disposition: Checking low-dimensional R-matrices does not control all pairs; finite versus infinite dimensional scope is material. No all-R mechanism or certified counterexample.
